children: State Bank of India (SBI) is developing products for Non-Resident Indian (NRI) customers who would like to deploy, say, $50,000 or $100,000, in India through GIFT City in foreign currency.
CS Setty, Chairman, said SBI has the largest International Banking Unit (IBU) in GIFT (Gujarat International Finance Tec) City. The IBU has a balance sheet of around $21 billion.

“We used GIFT City extensively for the FCNR(B) opportunity (whereby RBI provided a special USD-INR Forex Swap facility for FCNR(B) deposits mobilised between June 8 and August 31) , with a significant part of the leverage being provided through our IBU. We have customers from jurisdictions such as the US, UAE and UK keeping money with our GIFT City branch,” he said.

Setty observed that GIFT City offers an interesting opportunity for attracting retail deposits. There are also considerable opportunities around both outbound and inbound investments and developing products for customers in the International Financial Services Centre.
The SBI Chief emphasised that SBI’s GIFT City IBU complements its domestic branches by offering good interest rates to customers for periods of less than one year.
Further, the tax advantage and the ecosystem in GIFT City help India’s largest bank to offer higher deposit rate to customers for short duration.

For example, on a US Dollar (USD) term deposit (TD) below $1 million and $1 million & above in the 6 months 1 day to 9 months tenor, the Bank’s GIFT City IBU is currently offering interest rate of 4.65 per cent and 4.75 per cent, respectively.

In the case of a USD below $1 million and $1 million & above in the 6 months 1 day to 9 months tenor, the Bank’s GIFT City IBU is offering interest rate of 4.85 per cent and 4.95 per cent, respectively.
In sharp contrast, the highest interest that SBI’s domestic branches currently offer on USD-denominated FCNR (B) deposits is 4.40 per cent for a tenor of one year to less than two years.

When Banks were allowed by RBI to mop up FCNR (B) deposits of 3-5 years tenor between June 8 and August 31, 2026 and swap the deposit proceeds with the central bank, SBI’s interest rates on these deposits ranged from 5.25 per cent to 6 per cent.

title: SBI developing GIFT City specific products for NRI customers, says Chairman Setty
